title: Parabolic Anderson Model on Sierpinski Gasket
page_description: Interactive level-8 parabolic Anderson model on the Sierpinski gasket with a continuous localized initial profile of unit mass.
model_caption: One realization of the Itô parabolic Anderson model with Neumann boundary conditions and space–time white noise. The initial condition is a nonnegative continuous harmonic hat of total mass one, supported on two adjacent level-2 cells (measure 2/9) and zero elsewhere.
reading_caption: Positivity: every saved positive-time snapshot is positive at all 9,843 graph vertices, including points outside the initial support. The ln u view reveals very small positive values; switch to u to inspect spatial peaks. This is a numerical illustration of strict positivity, not a proof for the continuum SPDE.
numerical_accuracy_note: Time-step sensitivity: comparing Δt with 2Δt gives a 30.8% relative weighted L² difference at the final time, or 4.1% after normalizing each profile by its total mass. The normalized difference reaches 15.8% over saved times. This path is a qualitative illustration; absolute amplitudes and individual peak locations remain sensitive to time resolution.
method_note: At time zero, 2,185 vertices are positive and 7,658 are exactly zero. The level-2 nodal hat equals 1 at x₀ and 0 at the other level-2 vertices, is harmonically extended within cells, and is multiplied by 27/2 for unit mass. Exact zeros have ln u = −∞ and are not assigned a finite logarithmic height or color. Positive values have no display floor. Both choices use the same driving noise, with only the initial condition changed. Peak / mean is max(u) / ∫u dμ; spatial concentration in these paths does not establish ensemble moment intermittency. The noise is white relative to dt μ(dx), with μ the normalized Hausdorff measure. The scheme preserves positivity in exact arithmetic; very small early tails are not quantitatively certified, and floating-point zeros should not be read as a propagation delay.
equation_accessible_text: The time derivative of u equals kappa times the Neumann gasket Laplacian of u plus lambda times u times space-time white noise.
